title: Ancestral property: can a son claim half?

scenes.dialogue: Your grandfather's property comes to your father. Can you, his son, call it ancestral property and sue for half of it, while your father is still alive?
A trial court said yes, and gave the son a half share. The High Court reversed it. Nearly thirty years after he sued, the Supreme Court has ruled. Who was right?
scenes.shown: A trial court said yes, and gave the son a half share. The High Court reversed it. Nearly 30 years after he sued, the Supreme Court has ruled. Who was right?

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On the sixth of November, Honourable Justice Augustine George Masih and Honourable Justice Sunita Agarwal ruled.
scenes.shown: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On 6 November, Honourable Justice Augustine George Masih and Honourable Justice Sunita Agarwal ruled.

scenes.dialogue: A grandfather died without a will. In nineteen ninety three, his daughter sued to divide his property. His grandson was born while that suit was pending.
scenes.shown: A grandfather died without a will. In 1993, his daughter sued to divide his property. His grandson was born while that suit was pending.

scenes.dialogue: On the third of February, nineteen ninety four, a compromise decree gave the boy's father a plot as his share. Three years later, the father sold it to two buyers.
scenes.shown: On 3 February 1994, a compromise decree gave the boy's father a plot as his share. Three years later, the father sold it to two buyers.

scenes.dialogue: The same year, through his mother, the minor son sued for half. A Chennai civil court agreed, but on the buyers' appeal, the High Court held the father was the absolute owner.
The son said he was a coparcener by birth, before the decree, so the father could not sell the son's share. The buyers said a grandson is not a Class One heir.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the Supreme Court decide? What a father inherits under Section Eight of the Hindu Succession Act is his own, not joint family property.
scenes.shown: Finally, what did the Supreme Court decide? What a father inherits under Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act is his own, not joint family property.

scenes.dialogue: The partition made the father's share his exclusive property. The grandfather had died before the son was born, so the son could not claim a share. The appeal was dismissed.
